title: Isolation, culture, and use of primary murine myoblasts in small-molecule screens
protocol: Dissect mice at 4 weeks of age.
Euthanize the mouse by CO2 asphyxiation.
Spray the hind limb area with 70% ethanol.
Make a horizontal incision on the lower abdominal area using Vannas scissors.
Pull down the skin to expose the hindlimb muscle.
Use dissecting scissors to cut off as much muscle tissue as possible.
Place harvested tissue in a 15 mL conical tube containing HBSS on ice until ready for digestion.
Discard the HBSS from isolated muscle tissue and wash once with fresh HBSS.
Transfer washed tissue to a petri dish on ice and mechanically sheer it with dissecting Vannas scissors until paste-like.
Weigh the sheered tissue and transfer mixture to a clean, pre-weighed 15 mL conical tube.
Add 2 mL of Dispase II and 2 mL of Collagenase II enzyme solutions for each gram weight of tissue.
Place the tube into a shaking water bath set to speed of 150 strokes/min at 37°C for 20 min.
Pipette solution up and down using a 10 mL pipette 20 times after 20 minutes.
Return the tube to the water bath for another 10 min.
Remove the tube and pipette solution up and down 20 times using a 5 mL pipette.
Add 4 mL of DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin (D10) to the enzyme cell mixture.
Filter the entire content through a 100 μM sterile filter into a 50 mL conical tube.
Filter the flow-through through a 40 μM sterile filter into a clean 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min to pellet cells.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Wash the remaining cell pellet in 4 mL D10.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Wash the remaining cell pellet in 4 mL of D10.
Transfer the cell mixture to a clean 15 mL conical tube.
Repeat washes with 4 mL of D10 three times for a total of five washes.
On the final wash, centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL of primary myoblast growth medium (PMGM growth medium) supplemented with fresh bFGF at a concentration of 1:10,000.
Aspirate gelatin from the pre-coated T25 flask.
Plate cell resuspension.
Culture for 48 hours for cellular expansion in a humidified 37°C incubator supplied with 5% CO2.
After 48 hours of expansion, coat a new T25 flask with 2% gelatin for at least an hour.
Incubate PBS and primary myoblast growth medium in a 37°C water bath for 30 minutes.
Remove the culture flask from the incubator and gently aspirate the culture medium.
Add 3 mL of PBS to the flask and let it sit at room temperature for 2 minutes.
Perform the negative selection purification method which takes advantage of the weak adherence properties of the myoblasts compared to fibroblasts.
Hold the cell culture flasks firmly in your hand.
Perform five firm taps gently hitting the flask against a hard surface on each side to dislodge the myoblasts while leaving fibroblasts attached to the plate surface.
Visualize cells under the microscope to confirm myoblast detachment (suspended small rounded circular cells).
Add 3 mL primary myoblast growth medium to the culture flasks with PBS and dislodged myoblasts, being mindful not to scrape the cell culture surface.
Transfer the entire content to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the suspended myoblasts at 300 ×g for 5 min to pellet the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Avoid touching or scraping the cell flask surface when collecting dislodged myoblasts.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of PMGM media supplemented with bFGF.
Return the resuspended cells to the incubator for continued expansion.
Maintain myoblast growth cultures and split them every 48 h using a 1:10 Trypsin to PBS solution.
Maintain myoblasts in the proliferative state by supplementing culture media with fresh bFGF when plating after each low trypsin split.
Ensure confluency does not exceed 50% to maintain myoblasts in the proliferative state.
Cryopreserve primary myoblasts at a very early passage (P1-P2) for future use.
Perform a 1:10 low trypsin: PBS split of the floxed myoblasts.
Seed myoblasts in PMGM growth media at a concentration of 4 × 10^5 cells on a T75 gelatin-coated flask in 15 mL PMGM media.
Culture for 24 hours in an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Calculate the desired Multiplicity of Infection (MOI) for your gene target.
Dilute 2.5 μL of stock GFP-expressing or Cre-expressing adenovirus (titer of 4 × 10^10 pfu/mL) to 1 mL pre-warmed PMGM growth medium.
Add the diluted adenovirus directly to a 15 mL myoblast T75 culture flask and gently shake the flask to distribute evenly.
Return the infected cell flask to the incubator and culture for an additional 72 hours.
Visualize Adeno GFP expression using a fluorescent microscope after 72 hours of viral incubation time.
Aspirate the viral cell culture media from the infected cells.
Rinse cells gently with 3 mL of PBS.
Remove the PBS.
Trypsinize the virus-treated myoblasts using 2 mL of a 1:10 Trypsin to PBS solution.
Collect the trypsinized cells and place in a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the collected cells at 300×g for 5 min to pellet.
Aspirate the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Take an aliquot of 1 × 10^5 myoblasts from Adeno GFP and Cre treatment groups.
Return remaining cells to the incubator for further expansion.
Centrifuge Adeno GFP and CRE myoblast aliquots at 300×g for 5 min to obtain cell pellets.
Confirm protein target knockout in these cells using western blot and/or qPCR with appropriate antibodies and primers.
Weigh two 4-week-old male Cox10Flox/Pax7CRE-ERT2 mice.
Administer tamoxifen or vehicle via intraperitoneal injections at a concentration of 30 mg/g body weight daily for 5 days.
Coat three 96-well plates with 100 μL of 2% gelatin per well for at least 1 h.
Remove the 2% gelatin from 96-well plates after an hour.
Trypsinize a T-75 flask of primary myoblasts using low trypsin split as described previously.
Seed 30 wells of control and 30 wells of knockout myoblasts in 200 μL/well of PMGM growth media at a concentration of 2.4 × 10^3 cells/well according to the layout.
Leave plates in the cell culture hood for 15 minutes at 37°C after seeding to allow myoblasts to settle briefly.
Culture plates for 24 hours in an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Calculate the amount of staining buffer needed: number of primary myoblast wells × 100 μL per well.
Prepare the staining buffer by adding 0.5 μL of Hoechst stock solution and 2 μL of PI stock solution per 1 mL of pre-warmed serum-free D10 media.
Remove 180 μL of culture medium from each cell plate with a multichannel pipette, leaving behind 20 μL to prevent the myoblasts from drying.
Add 100 μL of staining buffer to each well containing myoblasts.
Incubate plates for 45 minutes at 37°C with 5% CO2 in the incubator.
Remove the cell plate from the incubator.
Perform the cell count using an automated cell counting instrument.
Record the myoblasts count labeled with Hoechst (Blue channel) and PI (Red Channel).
Calculate the live cell number as: Hoechst-stained cell number – PI-stained cell number for the control and KO myoblasts.
Replace medium in the remaining two 96-well plates.
Slowly remove 180 μL of culture medium with a multichannel pipette, leaving 20 μL behind.
Replace it with 180 μL of fresh PMGM growth media.
Incubate for an additional 48 h.
Repeat steps to record the dynamic range of the control and knockout myoblasts for Day 3 and Day 5 timepoints.
Determine which culture timepoint gives the maximal dynamic range.
Never aspirate culture media using a vacuum manifold when in a 96-well format.
Place 200 μL of PBS in the wells surrounding the perimeter of the 96-well plate to minimize edge effects.
Coat two 96-well plates with 2% gelatin according to the guidelines outlined in step 32.
Remove the gelatin after 1 hour.
Seed 2.4 × 10^3 flox control and knockout myoblasts per well in 100 μL of PMGM supplemented with bFGF according to the plate layout.
Incubate myoblasts for 24 h at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Expose KO myoblasts to a unique small biomolecule by administering it directly into the well.
Determine compound concentration empirically, starting typically at 10–25 μM.
Test each small biomolecule in duplicate according to the plate layout.
Gently swirl the cell culture plate after compound administration to ensure even distribution.
Return the plates to the incubator for a culture period of 5 days or as per the experimental endpoint defined in section “Establishing Dynamic Range”.
Assess the rescue potential of small biomolecules by measuring myoblast regenerative capacity following steps 35–39.
Calculate the fold rescue potential of each small biomolecule according to the equation provided.
Perform downstream concentration dose response analyses to identify the optimal drug concentration.
Conduct time course analyses to define drug dynamics.
Count cells 3 hours post-seeding using phase-contrast scan on an automated cell counter.
Use counted values to confirm even seeding of myoblasts.
Utilize counted values for normalization purposes.
Seed 96-well culture plates as desired for high-throughput screening.
